newsitem.title: USA: Talks on for Tuesday between WHX, USW.
newsitem.headline: Talks on for Tuesday between WHX, USW.

text.p: Contract negotiations were scheduled to resume Tuesday between the United Steelworkers union and WHX Corp, where a strike now in its seventh month is the longest in the U.S. steel industry in a decade, union officials said Monday.
Chief negotiators for the company and union are scheduled to meet at an undisclosed location, union spokesman Charles Robideau said.
The negotiations originally were to take place in a Pittsburgh hotel but were changed.
"The reason they were changed is because (the location) was leaked and (negotiators) didn't want a lot of hullabaloo about it," Robideau said.
The two sides agreed to meet after being invited to the bargaining table by U.S. Sen. Jay Rockefeller, D-W.Va. Robideau said Rockefeller will be present at the talks.
Union and company negotiators met last month but talks broke off after WHX announced it planned to sell or close two plants and a division involved in the work stoppage.
Some 4,500 steelworkers have been on strike against WHX since October 1.
The strike has idled eight steel plants in Pennsylvania, West Virginia and Ohio.
The strike centers around pensions. The union wants WHX to establish a defined benefit plan under which payments are guaranteed and are not based on age and hours worked.
WHX, however, wants to enhance its current defined contribution plan, under which contributions are put into an investment pool and are based on age and hours worked.
The company has maintained that it cannot afford a defined benefit plan and that such a plan could force it into bankruptcy.
The union wants WHX to use its $400 million in cash-on-hand to fund a defined benefit plan. The company has said it needs the cash to pay down debt and fund capital expenditures.
WHX has made a $45 per share hostile bid for Dynamics Corp of America.
